newsitem.title: USA: GM, UAW settle Oklahoma strike.
newsitem.headline: GM, UAW settle Oklahoma strike.

text.p: General Motors Corp. and the United Auto Workers reached a tentative accord to settle a seven-week strike at the company's Oklahoma City, Oklahoma, car plant, a company spokesman said on Sunday.
GM spokesman James Farmer said the agreement was reached late on Saturday night. Union officials at UAW Local 1999 could not be reached for comment.
About 3,500 UAW members struck the plant at midnight April 4 when the two sides could not reach agreement on a new local contract.

GM said earlier this month the Oklahoma City strike and a second, still unresolved, walkout at its Pontiac East truck plant in Pontiac, Michigan, had cost it $225 million in lost profits as of May 15.

The strike choked off supplies of GM's new Chevrolet Malibu, a crucial part of its bid to recapture market share in the key mid-size car segment. GM scaled back its Malibu advertising as a result of the walkout.
The plant also makes the redesigned Oldsmobile Cutlass.

UAW members demanded GM add about 500 jobs to help restore positions lost to retirements. The company stressed it needs competitive staffing levels in order to keep costs down. Details of the agreement were not released.
